payload.rationale: Cleveland travels to Tampa Bay for a Week 2 game. Both teams are 0-1, but the Week 1 results diverge: Cleveland lost 10-34 (-24 net), a lopsided defeat suggesting continued offensive struggles, while Tampa Bay lost a competitive 27-33 game (-6 net). Background priors matter more than one game: Tampa Bay has been a consistently competitive team in recent seasons with an established veteran quarterback and playoff pedigree, whereas Cleveland has been among the league's weaker teams, especially on offense, and appears to be in a rebuilding phase. Home-field advantage adds roughly 2-3 points to Tampa's edge. The injury report is fairly neutral: Cleveland is missing G Teven Jenkins and has CB Tyson Campbell questionable; Tampa has WR Jalen McMillan, CB Jacob Parrish, and S Miles Killebrew questionable. Neither list contains a franchise-altering absence. Putting this together, Cleveland projects as a clear road underdog, consistent with roughly a 28-33% win probability, and I settle near 30%. Reasons this could be too high: the Week 1 blowout may reflect a genuinely poor Cleveland roster/quarterback situation, and Tampa's home advantage plus offensive firepower could make this closer to a 22-25% proposition. Reasons this could be too low: single-game results are noisy, Tampa's defense allowed 33 points and may have real weaknesses, Cleveland's defense has been strong in recent years, and NFL upsets by 6-7 point underdogs occur roughly a third of the time; Tampa's questionable secondary players could also matter.
limitations: Only one game of 2026 data; team strength inferred largely from prior-season priors that may be outdated (roster and coaching changes unknown).
No final inactive lists, quarterback status confirmation, or weather information available.
No fitted power-rating model; estimate is judgment-based.
Tie outcomes settle at 0.50 under contract rules but are treated as non-wins here; ties are rare (~0.3%).
